items.resolution: A node listing returns each directory entry exactly once — no duplicates (single ReadDir pass; dedup impossible by construction).
Listing an empty directory returns entries:[] with status:'ok' — empty list + ok is the real-empty signal, never an error.
Entries are returned in lexical order (same comparator as the existing folder browser), stable across repeated calls.

items.resolution: At the listing cap (500): exactly 500 entries → truncated:false; 501+ → first 500 in lexical order + truncated:true.
Requesting the browsable root itself lists the root's children; a path resolving outside the root is rejected with the byte-identical traversal response.

items.resolution: Order of entries listed through symlinks is identical to direct listings — os.Root resolves containment, it does not reorder.
Entry names are returned verbatim — no truncation, no case folding, no Unicode normalization; names feed no numeric computation.
hidden=1 includes dot-prefixed entries at the root and at every depth; without it they are excluded.
Only dot-prefixed names are hidden ('.hidden' hidden, 'hidden' visible); mixed directories list both classes, separated only by the flag.
An empty directory returns entries:[] with and without hidden=1 — the flag never fabricates entries.
Entry order is identical with and without hidden=1 — the flag filters, never reorders.
Hidden-entry visibility agrees between the tree listing and the existing folder browser: same dot-prefix rule, byte-identical names.

A stored list containing both an ancestor and its descendant normalizes to the ancestor alone (per-class pruning: includes elide includes, excludes elide excludes; a root include + branch exclude coexist).

Normalizing an empty input list yields an empty result; at the PATCH boundary an empty list still means exactly auto-detection (legacy clients), while a tree-source empty selection is refused with code:'empty-selection'.
Normalization output is canonically ordered (deterministic sort) so equal selections produce byte-identical stored sets.
Normalizing an already-normalized set returns it unchanged (pure function — no hidden state, safe to run twice).
Saves serialize through the owned setter under settingsMu: last completed write wins, readers never observe partial state.

items.resolution: Sibling keep-lists (adjacent, non-nested) are all preserved — only strict descendants are elided; ticking two siblings stores both.
Starting from nothing checked normalizes to an empty set, which the PATCH guard treats per INTEG-04 semantics (tree-source refused with code:'empty-selection') — no special-cased whitelist path.
Ticking order does not affect the normalized result (pure normalization; any input order yields the same canonical set).

A stored path exactly equal to a snapshot Path matches exactly (equality before prefix logic); a stored descendant of a snapshot Path matches by the ancestor clause; when multiple snapshot Paths prefix a stored path, the LONGEST prefix wins — never the first component.
Empty intersection between stored paths and snapshot Paths aborts the restore BEFORE any destructive teardown, with an explicit 'nothing to restore for this item from this snapshot' error.
Each unmapped stored path is skipped individually with a scrubbed logged reason recorded in the restore result — skips are deterministic (stored-list order) and never abort the run.
